text: Proposition 4.1 (Anchored Softmax Approximation of Stationary Policies) . Let ${\mathbb{M}}$ be a finite MDP with an initial distribution $\min_{{s}\in{\mathcal{S}}}\mu_{0}({s})>0$ , and fix a reference action ${a}_{0}\in{\mathcal{A}}$ . Consider the anchored tabular logits $\psi({s},{a}_{0};\theta)=0$ and $\psi({s},{a};\theta)=\theta_{{s},{a}}$ for ${a}\neq{a}_{0}$ , with parameter space $\Theta_{R}=[-R,R]^{{\mathcal{S}}\times({\mathcal{A}}\setminus\{{a}_{0}\})}$ . For every stationary policy $\pi^{*}\in\Pi$ , including deterministic ones, and every ${\varepsilon}\in(0,1]$ , there exist $R={\OOSym\!\left(\log(\left|{\mathcal{A}}\right|/{\varepsilon})\right)}$ and a parameter $\theta\in\Theta_{R}$ such that $\displaystyle\max_{{s}\in{\mathcal{S}}}\;\lVert\pi_{\theta}(\,\cdot\,{}|{s})-\pi^{*}(\,\cdot\,{}|{s})\rVert_{1}\leq{\varepsilon},$ i.e. the family of anchored tabular softmax classes $\bigcup_{R>0}\{\pi_{\theta}:\theta\in\Theta_{R}\}$ is dense in the set of stationary policies.

Assumption 5.1 (Softmax-Parametrization) . The function $\psi:{\mathcal{S}}\times{\mathcal{A}}\times\Theta\to{\mathbb{R}}$ satisfies $\psi\in C^{2}({\mathcal{S}},{\mathcal{A}},\Theta;{\mathbb{R}})$ , and there exist constants ${\ell_{\psi}},{L_{\psi}}>0$ such that (i) $\max_{{s}\in{\mathcal{S}},{a}\in{\mathcal{A}}}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\lVert\nabla_{\theta}\psi({s},{a},\theta)\rVert\leq{\ell_{\psi}}$ and (ii) $\max_{{s}\in{\mathcal{S}},{a}\in{\mathcal{A}}}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\lVert\nabla^{2}_{\theta}\psi({s},{a},\theta)\rVert\leq{L_{\psi}}$ .

Assumption 5.2 (Occupancy-Measure Parametrization) . The parameter-to-occupancy mapping $\lambda:\Theta\to\Lambda$ , $\theta\mapsto\lambda^{\pi_{\theta}}$ , satisfies: • (Locally Invertible) For every parameter $\theta\in\Theta$ there exists a neighborhood $\theta\in\mathcal{U}_{\theta}\subset\Theta$ such that $\lambda^{\pi_{\theta}}|_{\mathcal{U}_{\theta}}$ is a bijection between $\mathcal{U}_{\theta}$ and ${\mathcal{V}}_{\theta}\coloneqq\lambda^{\pi_{\theta}}(\mathcal{U}_{\theta})$ . A (local) inverse is $\lambda^{-1}_{{\mathcal{V}}_{\theta}}:{\mathcal{V}}_{\theta}\to\mathcal{U}_{\theta}$ . • (Lipschitz Inverse) The inverse $\lambda^{-1}_{{\mathcal{V}}_{\theta}}$ is ${\mu_{\lambda}}$ -Lipschitz continuous over $\Theta.$ • (Locally Hidden Convex) There exists an ${\varepsilon}_{\lambda}>0$ such that for all ${\varepsilon}\in(0,{\varepsilon}_{\lambda}]$ and all $\theta\in\Theta$ the convex combination satisfies $(1-{\varepsilon})\lambda^{\pi_{\theta}}+{\varepsilon}\lambda^{\pi^{\star}}\in{\mathcal{V}}_{\theta}$ .

Theorem 5.4 (Biased SGD for ( PEN )) . Let ${\varepsilon}>0$ be the target accuracy. Under Assumptions 5.1 , 5.2 , 5.3 , running Section 5 with a step size $\eta=\nicefrac{{1}}{{L_{P,\theta}}}$ , a batch size of $B={\OOTildeSym\!\left(\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}^{2}}+\frac{\beta^{2}}{{\varepsilon}^{2}}\right)}$ and a trajectory length of $H={\OOSym\!\left(\log\left(\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}+\frac{\beta}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\right)}$ , we obtain $\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[P^{\mathsf{opt}}_{2,\beta}({\theta}^{(N)})\right]\leq{\varepsilon}\quad\text{after}\quad N\geq{\OOSym\!\left(\left(\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}+\frac{\beta}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot\log\left(\frac{P^{\mathsf{opt}}_{2,\beta}({\theta}^{(0)})}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\right)}={\OOTildeSym\!\left(\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}+\frac{\beta}{{\varepsilon}}\right)}.$ iterations, where $P^{\mathsf{opt}}_{2,\beta}({\theta}^{(0)})$ is the initial value gap and $L_{P,\theta}$ is defined in Corollary 0.B.4 .

Corollary 5.6 . Let ${\varepsilon}>0$ be the target accuracy. Under Assumptions 5.1 , 5.2 , 5.3 and strong duality, Assumption 5.5 , running Section 5 with a step size $\eta={\OOSym\!\left({\varepsilon}\right)}$ , a batch size of $B={\OOSym\!\left({{\varepsilon}^{-4}}\right)}$ , a penalty parameter $\beta={\OOSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-1}\right)}$ , and a trajectory length of $H={\OOSym\!\left(\log\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\right)}$ , we obtain $\displaystyle-{\varepsilon}\leq{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[F_{1}({\theta}^{(N)})-{F^{*}}\right]\leq{\varepsilon}\quad\text{and}\quad{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[[F_{2}({\theta}^{(N)})]_{+}\right]\leq{\varepsilon}$ after $N={\OOTildeSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-2}\right)}$ iterations, resulting in a total of ${\OOTildeSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-6}\right)}$ trajectory rollouts of length ${\OOSym\!\left(\log\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\right)}$ . 3 3 3 The expectation is with respect to the randomness of the MDP, the policy, and the initial state distribution.

Corollary 0.B.4 (Gradient Bound and Smoothness of Penalty Function) . Let Assumption 5.1 and Assumption 5.3 hold. Theorem 0.C.2 (Final Complexity Guarantee under Anchored Direct Softmax Parametrization) . Let $\lambda^{*}$ be the occupancy measure of an optimal stationary, potentially deterministic policy $\pi^{*}\in\Pi$ of ( CME ). Let ${\varepsilon}>0$ be the target accuracy. Under Assumption 5.3 for the constraint and strong duality, and using the anchored direct-softmax parametrization on $\Theta_{R}=[-R,R]^{{\mathcal{S}}\times({\mathcal{A}}\setminus\{{a}_{0}\})}$ , run Section 5 with a step size $\eta={\OOSym\!\left({\varepsilon}\right)}$ , a batch size $B={\OOSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-4}\right)}$ , a penalty parameter $\beta={\OOSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-1}\right)}$ , and a trajectory length $H={\OOSym\!\left(\log(1/{\varepsilon})\right)}$ . Then $\displaystyle-{\varepsilon}\leq{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[{\mathcal{H}}(\lambda^{\pi_{{\theta}^{(N)}}})-{\mathcal{H}}(\lambda^{*})\right]\leq{\varepsilon},\qquad{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[[{\mathcal{R}}(\lambda^{\pi_{{\theta}^{(N)}}})]_{+}\right]\leq{\varepsilon}$ after $N={\OOTildeSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-2}\right)}$ iterations, resulting in a total of ${\OOTildeSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-6}\right)}$ trajectory rollouts of length ${\OOSym\!\left(\log(1/{\varepsilon})\right)}$ .

Definition 0.D.1 (Hidden Convexity) . The above problem ( HC ) is called hidden convex with modulus $\mu_{c}>0$ , if its components satisfy the following underlying conditions. 1. The domain ${\Lambda}=c({\Theta})$ is convex, the functions $H_{1},H_{2}:{\Lambda}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ are convex, i.e. satisfy for $i=1,2$ and for all $u,v\in{\Lambda}$ and any $\alpha\in[0,1]$ $\displaystyle H_{i}((1-\alpha){u}+\alpha{v})\leq(1-\alpha)H_{i}({u})+\alpha H_{i}({v})-\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha\mu_{H}}{2}\lVert{u}-{v}\rVert^{2}.$ (HC-1) Additionally, we assume ( HC ) admits a solution ${u}^{*}\in{\Lambda}$ with its corresponding objective function value ${F^{*}}\coloneqq H_{1}({u}^{*})=F_{1}(c^{-1}({u}^{*}))$ . Throughout this appendix, ${F^{*}}$ denotes the minimum which corresponds to $-{F^{*}}$ from ( CME ). 2. The map $c:{\Theta}\to{\Lambda}$ is invertible and there exists a $\mu_{c}>0$ such that for all ${\theta},{\tilde{\theta}}\in{\Theta}$ it holds $\displaystyle\lVert c({\theta})-c({\tilde{\theta}})\rVert\geq\mu_{c}\lVert{\theta}-{\tilde{\theta}}\rVert.$ (HC-2) If $\mu_{H}>0$ , we refer to ( HC ) as $(\mu_{c},\mu_{H})$ -strongly convex. Note that in this more generic setting, we have $\mu_{c}=\nicefrac{{1}}{{\mu_{\lambda}}}$ of Assumption 5.2 . We can map ( CME ) to ( HC ) via $H_{1}=-{\mathcal{H}}$ and $H_{2}={\mathcal{R}}$ .

Proposition 0.D.2 ( Fatkhullin et al. [44] Prop. 3) . Let $F_{i}(\,\cdot\,{})$ , $i=1,2$ , be hidden convex with $\mu_{c}>0$ . For any $\alpha\in[0,1]$ and ${\theta},{\tilde{\theta}}\in{\Theta}$ , define ${\theta}_{\alpha}\coloneqq c^{-1}((1-\alpha)c({\theta})+\alpha c({\tilde{\theta}}))$ , then, for $i=1,2$ , the following functional inequality $\displaystyle F_{i}({\theta}_{\alpha})\leq(1-\alpha)F_{i}({\theta})+\alpha F_{i}({\tilde{\theta}})-\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha\mu_{H}}{2}\lVert c({\theta})-c({\tilde{\theta}})\rVert^{2},$ (HC-FI) and norm inequality $\displaystyle\lVert{\theta}_{\alpha}-{\theta}\rVert\leq\frac{\alpha}{\mu_{c}}\lVert c({\theta})-c({\tilde{\theta}})\rVert.$ (HC-NI) hold.

Theorem 0.D.3 (Biased SGD, Hidden Convexity) . Let $F$ be $L$ -smooth and hidden convex with ${F^{*}}\coloneqq F({\theta}^{*})$ for an ${\theta}^{*}\in{\Theta}$ , i.e. $F_{2}\equiv 0$ . Then running (projected) biased ( SGD ), with a step size $\eta\leq\frac{1}{L}$ , yields for every $K\in{\mathbb{N}}$ and any $\alpha\in[0,1]$ the following inequality $\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[F({\theta}^{(N+1)})-{F^{*}}\right]\leq(1-\alpha)^{N}\Delta_{0}+\frac{{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{{\mu^{2}_{c}}\eta}\alpha+\frac{\eta}{2}\frac{1}{\alpha}\left(\sigma^{2}+\delta^{2}\right)$ with $\Delta_{0}\coloneqq{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[F({\theta}^{(0)})-{F^{*}}\right]$ . In particular, for an arbitrary target accuracy of ${\varepsilon}>0$ , without loss of generality ${\varepsilon}\leq\frac{3{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}L}{{\mu^{2}_{c}}}$ , by picking $\displaystyle\alpha\leq\frac{{\mu^{2}_{c}}\eta}{{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}\frac{{\varepsilon}}{3}\leq\frac{{\mu^{2}_{c}}}{{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}L}\frac{{\varepsilon}}{3}$ after $\displaystyle N\geq\frac{1}{\alpha}\log\left(\frac{3\Delta_{0}}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\geq\frac{3{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}\cdot L}{{\mu^{2}_{c}}}\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\log\left(\frac{3\Delta_{0}}{{\varepsilon}}\right)$ steps, the last iterate satisfies $\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[F({\theta}^{(N+1)})-{F^{*}}\right]\leq\frac{2{\varepsilon}}{3}+\frac{\eta}{2}\frac{1}{\alpha}\left(\sigma^{2}+\delta^{2}\right).$ Consequently, we need the bias and the variance to satisfy $\displaystyle\sigma^{2},\delta^{2}\leq\frac{{\varepsilon}}{3}\frac{\alpha}{\eta}\leq\frac{{\mu^{2}_{c}}}{9{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{\varepsilon}^{2}$ in order to get ${\varepsilon}$ -close to the global minima.

Assumption 0.D.4 . We conduct our analysis under the following (standard) assumptions: • (Weak Convexity) $F_{1},F_{2}$ to be $\rho$ -weakly convex, for an $\rho>0$ . It is known that weak convexity is a relatively mild assumption, compared to e.g. smoothness [ 29 , 40 ] . $F_{i}$ is weakly convex, if e.g. $F_{i}$ is twice continuously differentiable with the Hessian satisfying $\nabla^{2}F_{i}({\theta})\succcurlyeq-\rho$ , for all ${\theta}\in{\Theta}$ , $i=1,2$ , cf. Prop 4.12 in Vial [115] . • (Bounded [Sub-]Gradients) The functions $F_{i}$ , $i=1,2$ , are continuous and satisfy for all ${\theta}\in{\Theta}$ that $\partial F_{i}({\theta})\neq\emptyset$ and with $\lVert g\rVert\leq G$ we have a uniform bound for all sub-gradients $g\in\partial F_{i}({\theta})$ , ${\theta}\in{\Theta}$ . • (Bounded Domain) The Domain ${\Lambda}$ has a bounded diameter ${\mathcal{D}_{\Lambda}}>0$ .

Assumption 0.D.5 (Unconstrained Solution Oracle) . We assume to have access to an inner approximate solution oracle ${\mathcal{A}}_{{{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}}$ to solve ( IPPPM ) to an ${{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}$ -accuracy in expectation for any ${{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}>0$ , i.e. $\displaystyle{{\varphi}^{(k)}_{\mathrm{pen}}}({\theta}^{(k)})-{{\varphi}^{(k)}_{\mathrm{pen}}}(\hat{{\theta}}^{(k)})\leq{{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}$ for all iterations $k\in[N]$ after ${T_{\mathrm{in}}}={T_{\mathrm{in}}}({{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}})$ steps.

Theorem 0.D.6 (PPPM, Penalty Function) . Let ( HC ) be hidden convex and Assumption 0.D.4 hold. Given a target precision ${\varepsilon}>0$ , a lifting parameter ${\hat{\rho}}>\rho_{\varphi}$ , assume ${\varepsilon}\leq\frac{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{2{\mu^{2}_{c}}}$ holds. Then after $N\in{\mathbb{N}}$ steps, the last iterate of Algorithm 2 satisfies $\displaystyle\begin{aligned} F_{1}({\theta}^{(N)})-{F^{*}}+\beta{{\mathcal{L}}(F_{2}({\theta}^{(N)}))}\leq{\varepsilon}\end{aligned}$ (OptGap) after $\displaystyle N\geq\frac{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{2{\mu^{2}_{c}}}\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\cdot\log\left(\frac{3(\Delta_{0}+\beta{\mathcal{V}_{0}})}{{\varepsilon}}\right)$ iterations, where $\Delta_{0}\coloneqq F_{1}({\theta}^{(0)})-{F^{*}}$ , ${\mathcal{V}_{0}}\coloneqq{{\mathcal{L}}(F_{2}({\theta}^{(0)}))}$ , an $\alpha\leq\frac{2{\mu^{2}_{c}}}{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{\varepsilon}\in[0,1]$ used in the analysis and a penalty parameter $\beta>1$ . With an inner precision of ${{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}\leq\frac{\alpha}{2}{\varepsilon}$ , the total sample complexity is given by $\displaystyle{T_{\mathrm{tot}}}\geq N\cdot{T_{\mathrm{in}}}\left({{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}\right)$ $\displaystyle=\frac{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{2{\mu^{2}_{c}}}\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\cdot\log\left(\frac{3(\Delta_{0}+\beta{\mathcal{V}_{0}})}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot{T_{\mathrm{in}}}\left({{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}\right).$

Remark 0.D.7 (Role of the Penalty Parameter) . It is important to emphasize that, although the parameter $\beta$ appears only logarithmically in the number of outer iterations $N$ , it plays a crucial role in shaping the properties of the penalty function. In particular, $\beta$ affects the norm of the (sub-)gradients, the associated smoothness constant, and consequently the weak convexity parameter. As a result, it directly influences the computational complexity of the inner solver employed for the subproblem.

Theorem 0.D.8 (PPPM, Exact Penalty) . We assume the assumptions of Theorem 0.D.6 and strong duality hold for ( HC ) with a Lagrangian multiplier ${\nu^{*}}\geq 0$ . Then, running Algorithm 2 with the exact penalty ${{\mathcal{L}}(\,\cdot\,{})}=[\,\cdot\,{}]_{+}$ and any $\beta\geq 2\cdot{\nu^{*}}+2$ yields following last iterate guarantee on the optimality gap and constraint violation $\displaystyle\left\lvert F_{1}({\theta}^{(N)})-{F^{*}}\right\rvert\leq{\varepsilon}\quad\text{and }\;[F_{2}({\theta}^{(N)})]_{+}\leq{\varepsilon}$ (IPPPM-Ex) after $\displaystyle N\geq\frac{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{2\mu_{c}^{2}}\frac{\beta}{{\varepsilon}}\cdot\log\left(\frac{3\beta[\Delta_{0}+\beta{\mathcal{V}_{0}}]}{{\varepsilon}}\right)$ iterations, where $\Delta_{0}\coloneqq F_{1}({\theta}^{(0)})-{F^{*}}$ , and ${\mathcal{V}_{0}}\coloneqq[F_{2}({\theta}^{(0)})]_{+}$ . With an inner precision ${{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}\leq\frac{\alpha}{2\beta}{\varepsilon}$ , where $\alpha\leq\frac{2\mu_{c}^{2}}{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{\varepsilon}\in[0,1]$ as in Theorem 0.D.6 , the total rate is given by $\displaystyle{T_{\mathrm{tot}}}$ $\displaystyle\geq N\cdot{T_{\mathrm{in}}}\left({{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}\right)=\frac{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{2\mu_{c}^{2}}\frac{\beta}{{\varepsilon}}\cdot\log\left(\frac{3\beta[\Delta_{0}+{\mathcal{V}_{0}}]}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot{T_{\mathrm{in}}}\left({{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}\right)$ $\displaystyle\geq\frac{3{\hat{\rho}}{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{2\mu_{c}^{2}}\frac{\beta}{{\varepsilon}}\cdot\log\left(\frac{3\beta[\Delta_{0}+{\mathcal{V}_{0}}]}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot{T_{\mathrm{in}}}\left(\frac{\alpha}{2\beta}{\varepsilon}\right)$

Corollary 0.D.12 (IPPPM+GD, Smooth, Quadratic Penalty) . Under the assumptions of Theorem 0.D.6 , and assuming that $F_{1},F_{2}$ are $L$ -smooth, running Algorithm 2 with the quadratic penalty ${{\mathcal{L}}(\,\cdot\,)}\coloneqq{[\,\cdot\,]_{+}^{2}}$ , ${\hat{\rho}}({\varepsilon})\coloneqq 2\rho_{\varphi}({\varepsilon})$ , and $\beta=\beta({\varepsilon})\coloneqq\frac{2({\nu^{*}}+1)^{2}}{{\varepsilon}}$ yields the guarantee $\displaystyle\left\lvert F_{1}({\theta}^{(N)})-{F^{*}}\right\rvert\leq{\varepsilon}\quad\text{and}\quad[F_{2}({\theta}^{(N)})]_{+}\leq{\varepsilon}.$ The total number of gradient evaluations when using the gradient descent (GD) method as the inner solver, is given by: $\displaystyle T_{\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{{sm}}}$ $\displaystyle=\frac{{\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Lambda}}}{\mu_{c}^{2}}\beta({\varepsilon})\cdot\log\left(3\beta({\varepsilon})[\Delta_{0}+\beta({\varepsilon}){\mathcal{V}_{0}}]\right)\cdot$ $\displaystyle\qquad\cdot L_{\varphi}({\varepsilon})\cdot\log\left(\frac{L_{\varphi}({\varepsilon}){\mathcal{D}^{2}_{\Theta}}}{{{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}}\right)$ $\displaystyle={\OOTildeSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-2}\right)},$ where $\Delta_{0}\coloneqq F_{1}({\theta}^{(0)})-{F^{*}}$ , ${\mathcal{V}_{0}}\coloneqq{[F_{2}({\theta}^{(0)})]_{+}^{2}}$ , $L_{\varphi}({\varepsilon})=L+{\hat{\rho}}+\beta({\varepsilon})\cdot G({\mathcal{D}_{\Theta}}L+G)={\OOSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-1}\right)}$ and $\rho_{\varphi}({\varepsilon})=\beta({\varepsilon})G{\mathcal{D}_{\Theta}}\cdot\min\{\rho,L\}={\OOSym\!\left({\varepsilon}^{-1}\right)}$ .

Theorem 0.D.14 (Hidden Strongly Convex, PPPM, Penalty Function) . Assume ( HC ) is hidden strongly convex with modulus $\mu_{H}>0$ and we have access to an oracle ${\mathcal{A}}$ according to Assumption 0.D.5 . For a target precision ${\varepsilon}>0$ , lifting parameter ${\hat{\rho}}>\rho$ , and a penalty parameter $\beta\geq 1$ . With the choice of $\alpha\coloneqq\frac{\mu_{c}^{2}\mu_{H}}{{\hat{\rho}}+\mu_{c}^{2}\mu_{H}}\in[0,1]$ and for $N\in{\mathbb{N}}$ , the last iterate of Algorithm 2 satisfies $\displaystyle P^{\mathsf{opt}}_{{\mathcal{L}},\beta}({\theta}^{(N)})=F_{1}({\theta}^{(N)})-{F^{*}}+\beta{{\mathcal{L}}(F_{2}({\theta}^{(N)}))}\leq{\varepsilon}$ after $\displaystyle N\geq\frac{{\hat{\rho}}+\mu_{c}^{2}\mu_{H}}{\mu_{c}^{2}\mu_{H}}\cdot\log\left(\frac{2(\Delta_{0}+\beta{\mathcal{V}_{0}})}{{\varepsilon}}\right)$ iterations, where $\Delta_{0}\coloneqq F_{1}(\hat{{\theta}}^{(k)})-{F^{*}}$ and ${\mathcal{V}_{0}}\coloneqq{{\mathcal{L}}(F_{2}({\theta}^{(0)}))}$ . With an inner precision of ${{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}}\leq\frac{\alpha{\varepsilon}}{2}$ , the total rate is in general given by $\displaystyle{T_{\mathrm{tot}}}\geq N\cdot{T_{\mathrm{in}}}({{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{in}}})=\frac{{\hat{\rho}}+\mu_{c}^{2}\mu_{H}}{\mu_{c}^{2}\mu_{H}}\cdot\log\left(\frac{2(\Delta_{0}+\beta{\mathcal{V}_{0}})}{{\varepsilon}}\right)\cdot{T_{\mathrm{in}}}\left(\frac{1}{2}\alpha{\varepsilon}\right).$
